title: Importer Worker
description: Messages, queues, dead letters, database, pods, versions and logs for importer-worker. Source: importer/k8s/dashboards/importer-worker.json

panels.title: Version
panels.description: Image tag the pods run now. Two values means a rollout is in progress.

panels.title: Ready pods
panels.description: Pods passing their readiness probe: consuming from RabbitMQ, and Postgres answers.

panels.title: Processed
panels.description: Messages handled successfully in the selected time range (including duplicates and deleted items, which need no work).

panels.title: Requeued
panels.description: Failed attempts that will be retried after a backoff (e.g. database down).

panels.title: Dead-lettered
panels.description: Messages given up on in the selected time range: malformed, or failed 10 times. They wait in the DLQ.

panels.title: p95 processing
panels.description: 95% of messages in the selected time range were processed faster than this, retry waits included.

panels.title: Waiting in queue
panels.description: Messages in the queue that no worker has taken yet. Should be about 0; growing means the workers can't keep up or aren't consuming.

panels.title: In DLQ
panels.description: Messages in the dead-letter queue, waiting for a human. Inspect them in the RabbitMQ management UI.

panels.title: Restarts
panels.description: Container restarts in the selected time range (crashes, OOM kills, failed liveness probes).

panels.title: Messages per second
panels.description: By outcome. done: acked. requeued: failed, retried after a backoff. dead_lettered: sent to the DLQ.

panels.title: Processing time
panels.description: Time per message, from delivery to ack. Requeued messages include the backoff wait (1s, 2s, 4s...).

panels.title: Queue
panels.description: importer-worker.item-created. ready: waiting for a worker. unacked: delivered to a worker (being processed or prefetched, up to 10 per pod).

panels.title: Consumers
panels.description: Workers consuming the queue: one per pod. Below the number of pods means a worker lost its connection.

panels.title: Dead-letter queue
panels.description: importer-worker.item-created.dlq. Anything here needs a look: the worker's error logs say why it gave up.

panels.title: API outbox backlog
panels.description: Events importer-api has saved but not published yet. Usually 0: if it grows, RabbitMQ is down or unreachable from the API, and the worker gets nothing.

panels.title: Recent messages (traces)
panels.description: The last 20 processed messages. Each trace starts at the API request that created the item, so it shows the whole path: request, publish, process, UPDATE.

panels.title: Database call duration (p95)
panels.description: query: running SQL (the UPDATE that marks an item done). acquire: waiting for a free connection. connect: opening a new connection.

panels.title: Database calls per second
panels.description: Includes the /readyz ping every 5s per pod. Errors in red.

panels.title: Connection pool
panels.description: Connections per pod. The worker handles one message at a time, so it rarely needs more than one.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: CPU cores used per pod. Near the limit (dashed), the container is throttled and gets slower.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Working set per pod, what the kernel counts against the limit (dashed). Reaching it gets the container OOM-killed.

panels.title: Restarts
panels.description: Container restarts. Check the logs around the bar, and `kubectl -n importer describe pod` for the reason (OOMKilled, liveness).

panels.title: Version history
panels.description: One row per version: colored while pods run it, the value is how many. Overlaps are rolling updates. Widen the time range to see older releases.

panels.title: Pod starts
panels.description: Every time a pod started and the version it ran (from its 'worker starting' log line).

panels.title: Log lines per second
panels.description: By level. WARN: a message was requeued or the RabbitMQ connection dropped. ERROR: a message went to the DLQ.

targets.expr: sum by (level) (rate({namespace="importer", container="importer-worker", pod=~"$pod"} | json level="level" [$__auto]))

panels.title: Errors and warnings
panels.description: Requeued and dead-lettered messages, with the reason. Expand a line and use 'View trace' to open it in Tempo.

panels.title: All logs
panels.description: Filter with the 'Search logs' box at the top, e.g. an item id: "item_id":42.
